Resolves #19305

`DomEvents` coalesces `mousemove` into the next animation frame but sent every other mouse event at once. A press that followed a jump in the same frame therefore reached the app worker as press-then-move. `Neo.canvas.Base#updateMouseState` derives movement from the last reported position, so the press carried the whole jump with `buttons: 1`, and `GraphScene` orbited on it. In the probe on engine `a50ae57ce8`, one click swung the camera from yaw 0.7 to 3.1. Now `flushPendingMouseMove` sends the waiting move before a press, release, click, double click, context menu, wheel, enter or leave. A wheel flushes only on the path that sends it: one the main thread keeps (no target, or inside its target's buffer) leaves the move to its frame. Moves on their own still send once per frame.

Evidence: L2 (unit, the main-thread handlers with stubbed frames and transport) → L2 required for AC-1 and AC-2. Residual: AC-3 (the Institution drops its NL pointer-rest workaround on an engine pin carrying this)
Residual-Owner: neomjs/neo-agent-institution#277

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `DomEvents.spec` › "every other mouse event sends a move still waiting for its frame first": for each of the eight handlers, the order is `mousemove` then the event. Red on dev (8 moves missing); a mutation dropping only the wheel's flush turns it red again |
| AC-2 | Same arm: two moves in one frame send one message, and a flushed move leaves nothing for its frame (16 messages after all frames run). "a wheel the main thread keeps leaves a waiting move to its frame": a move, a kept wheel and a move in one frame send only the second move, for a wheel without a target and for one inside its target's buffer. Red on `871157fde1` (the first move flushed); a mutation flushing before the buffer check turns the buffer half red again |
| AC-3 | post-merge (below) |
